parts.title: Part 1 — Photography course enquiry
parts.subtitle: 2 speakers, phone enquiry, easiest
parts.instructions: Questions 1–10. Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

script.speaker: WOMAN (staff)
script.text: Riverside Arts Centre, good afternoon, how can I help you?

script.speaker: MAN (caller)
script.text: Hi, I saw a flyer about a photography course and wanted to find out more.

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: Of course. That'll be our Introduction to Digital Photography course, that's D-I-G-I-T-A-L, Digital Photography, for complete beginners.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: Perfect, that's exactly what I'm after. When does it run?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: Classes are every Tuesday evening.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: Tuesday, got it. And what time does it start?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: We begin at six... actually, sorry, let me check that again... yes, six fifteen, so 6.15pm.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: 6.15, thanks. And how long does the course run for altogether?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: It's an eight week course, so eight sessions in total.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: Eight weeks, great. What's the fee?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: The full course is four thousand five hundred dinars, that's 4,500 DA.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: 4,500, okay. Does that include any equipment, or do I need my own camera?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: It actually includes the use of a camera for the duration of the course, there's just a small refundable deposit required.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: Oh brilliant, that's useful, I don't own one yet. Which room will it be in?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: You'll be in Studio 3.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: Studio 3. And whereabouts is that in the building?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: That's on the first floor, just past the reception area.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: First floor, got it. Is there anything I should bring to the first session?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: Just a notebook for taking notes, everything else is provided.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: A notebook, okay, easy enough. And if I book today, will I get a reference number?

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: Yes, every booking reference begins with the letters R-A-C, followed by four digits.

script.speaker: MAN
script.text: RAC, understood. Thanks very much for your help.

script.speaker: WOMAN
script.text: You're welcome, enjoy the course!

parts.title: Part 2 — Talk to new volunteers
parts.subtitle: 1 speaker, monologue to new volunteers
parts.instructions: Questions 11–20. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C, or the correct letters for multi-select and matching questions.

script.speaker: SPEAKER
script.text: Good evening everyone, and thank you for coming along tonight. Before we start, I do apologise, I know some of the chairs are placed a little close together, we had a much smaller room booked originally so do feel free to shuffle round and make yourselves comfortable.

script.speaker: SPEAKER
script.text: So, a little about who volunteers with us. People sometimes assume we're looking for young, energetic volunteers only, but honestly, age matters far less to us than reliability, we've had wonderful volunteers in their twenties and in their seventies, what matters is that we can count on you turning up when you say you will.

script.speaker: SPEAKER
script.text: In terms of training, it isn't just a single session and then you're on your own, that first session covers the basics, but training actually continues well after that, with refresher sessions and on the job guidance from our more experienced volunteers.

script.speaker: SPEAKER
script.text: Now, before you apply, there are really two things we'd like you to think seriously about. First, your level of commitment, we need people who can stick with a role for at least six months, and second, your availability, particularly whether you can commit to the same day or two each week.

script.speaker: SPEAKER
script.text: Let me run through the different roles we have. If you enjoy being outdoors and active, dog walking is a great fit, since it really does require a good level of physical fitness, you'll be out for an hour or more at a time. For the reception desk, we're mainly looking for someone comfortable with basic computer skills, you'll be logging visitors and updating our booking system. Fundraising events need volunteers who have comfort speaking to the public, you'll be approaching people directly to explain what we do. If cats are more your thing, cat socialising calls for patience and a calm manner above all, since nervous cats need a gentle, unhurried approach. And finally, if you'd like to help with our adoption listings, that role really depends on having a good camera or phone, since clear photographs make a huge difference to how quickly an animal finds a home.

parts.title: Part 3 — Food-waste survey discussion
parts.subtitle: 2 speakers, Tom and Sara, discussing a food-waste survey
parts.instructions: Questions 21–30. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C, or the correct letters for multi-select questions.

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: Sorry I'm a bit late, Sara, I actually couldn't find anywhere to park, the whole car park was full.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: No worries, I only just got here myself. So, shall we go through the lecturer's comments on our food waste report?

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: Yeah. Honestly, the bit that surprised me most was learning that most of the cafeteria's waste doesn't actually come from what students leave on their plates, it's mostly unsold food that never even gets eaten.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: I know, I assumed it'd be the opposite. Anyway, what did you think of the feedback overall?

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: It stung a bit, but I think it was accurate, if unwelcome, if I'm honest with myself.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: Same. Though I will say, I don't think we fully agree on the careers advice session we complained about earlier this year.

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: What do you mean? I thought we were on the same page there.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: Well, we both agreed it was a problem, but we disagreed about exactly what was wrong with it, you thought it was too generic, I thought it just came too late in the year.

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: Ah, fair point, that's true actually.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: And speaking of careers, have you given more thought to what you want to do?

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: A bit. Though we still don't agree on when to commit to a particular path, you think I should decide now, I'd rather keep my options open a while longer.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: That's fair enough. How's the internship going, by the way?

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: Good, though it's made me realise how common unpaid work experience is in this industry. I've just come to accept it as simply how things are, even if it's not ideal.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: I used to feel that way too. Looking back at my own internship, I'll admit I made a couple of mistakes, I worried far too much about how I came across to everyone, and I expected too much responsibility too soon, which frustrated me when it didn't happen.

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: That's really useful to know, thanks. Anyway, for the follow up survey, what else should we ask students?

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: I think we should find out why customers leave food on their plates in the first place, that still isn't clear from this data.

script.speaker: TOM
script.text: Good idea. And maybe also what time of day most of the unsold food gets thrown away, that could help the cafeteria plan portions better.

script.speaker: SARA
script.text: Yes, let's add both of those.

parts.title: Part 4 — Rewilding project lecture
parts.subtitle: 1 speaker, lecture on a rewilding project
parts.instructions: Questions 31–40. Complete the summary below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Good morning everyone. Today I want to talk about one of the most successful rewilding projects in the region, the return of beavers to our local river system.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Beavers were hunted to extinction here over a century ago, largely for their fur, but also for a glandular substance called castoreum, which was once highly valued in perfumery and medicine.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Without beavers shaping the landscape, the river gradually lost its natural ability to manage flooding, since the dams and wetlands beavers create had always acted as a kind of natural buffer during heavy rainfall.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Before any animals were introduced, the project team spent two full years recording a baseline of the existing wildlife in the area, so that any future changes could be properly measured against it.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: The beavers themselves came from a wild population in a neighbouring country, where numbers had recovered enough to allow a small number to be relocated.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Once they arrived, the animals were kept in quarantine for several weeks before release, purely as a precaution, to make sure none of them were carrying disease.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Each beaver was also fitted with a tracking collar, so the team could follow their movements and check on how well they were settling into their new territory.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Within just a couple of years, the dams they built were already slowing the flow of water during storms, reducing the kind of sudden flooding that used to affect farmland downstream.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: The still, calm pools that formed behind the dams also supported noticeably more insect life, which in turn benefited fish and birds further up the food chain.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: As word spread locally, the project saw a real rise in tourism too, with visitors coming specifically to see the dams and, if they're lucky, the beavers themselves at dawn or dusk.

script.speaker: LECTURER
script.text: Looking ahead, the team's main priority now is securing long-term funding, since monitoring a project like this properly doesn't stop once the animals are released, it really only just begins.
